audit:Content audit of the level-up bili.currentState:
The seeded L5 level (src/content/data/general-l5.json, ~325KB) is genuinely high-quality, expert-voiced content that mostly clears the "must not look AI-generated" bar. It is 100% General-track: 36 items, 9 modules, 3 Rooms, 2 Field Work — every single record has track:"general" (grep for track:"ai" returns nothing anywhere in src/content/data or research/). The AI track is not a skeleton; it is entirely absent.

Technical accuracy is strong and current. The consistency modules (m1-m2) correctly separate recency (linearizability) from isolation (serializability) as orthogonal axes, correctly define strict serializability as their conjunction, cite Jepsen/Kleppmann, and use write-skew/on-call as the anchor example — this is accurate and at real Staff depth. PACELC, transactional outbox, idempotent-receiver vs "exactly-once is a myth," saga choreography-vs-orchestration, cache stampede (single-flight + soft/hard TTL + negative caching), SLI/SLO/SLA + error budget as release throttle, and wide-events-over-three-pillars are all correct and framed as opinionated judgment, not listicle. The "leadership" modules (m6-m9) draw on real named sources — Larson's snacking/preening/chasing-ghosts, Squarespace "yes/if" approver model, Bezos two-way-doors, Lara Hogan sponsorship-vs-mentorship, Tanya Reilly "Being Glue" — used substantively, not name-dropped.

The CBM quiz items are the strongest asset: distractors map to real, named misconceptions with per-option rationales explaining why each wrong answer is wrong (e.g. gen-l5-a1-04 payment double-charge: the "exactly-once queue" and "wrap in a transaction" distractors are exactly what mid-level engineers actually propose). The 3 Rooms (SJT) are well-keyed with a 3/1/0/-2 scoring rubric and defensible rationales. The Field Work "30% Gauntlet" (gen-l5-fw-gauntlet) is excellent: a real Express+pg+Anthropic endpoint with genuinely planted bugs (SQL string-interpolation injection on accountId AND summary, prompt-injection via note concatenated into system prompt + tool implications, missing idempotency guard, unbounded query/p99 cliff, catch that returns 200 ok:true summary:null) matched to a weighted rubric.

Bilingual quality is high. ES reads as idiomatic native Spanish, not MT: "de guardia" (not "on-call" calque), "padrinazgo sobre mentoría," "pegamento estratégico" for glue work, "fiabilidad," "juicio de compromisos." No "librería"-for-library-only issue (appears 2x but acceptably), no "actualmente"/"soportar"/"realizar" false-friend calques (0 occurrences). Files are clean UTF-8 (terminal mojibake was display-only; verified chars are U+00E1 á, U+00F3 ó, U+00BF ¿, U+2014 —).

items.spec: globals.css has ZERO @keyframes and src/ has no IntersectionObserver — the audit's #1 gap to award-worthy. Ship: (a) a motion token set in CSS custom props (--ease-out-expo: cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1) for reveals; --ease-spring: cubic-bezier(0.34,1.56,0.64,1) for reward affordances; --dur-1:120ms/--dur-2:200ms/--dur-3:320ms) and never hardcode timing again; (b) a tiny useReveal IntersectionObserver hook → staggered fade+translateY(8px→0) with per-item transition-delay: calc(var(--i)*60ms), applied to proof band, track cards, method rows, stat tiles (page.tsx); (c) a count-up hook for every mono readout (Radar % Radar.tsx:119, MeView Signal/counts MeView.tsx:105, FieldWork score FieldWorkView.tsx:83). Encode the five placement bands (+ archetype) into a URL hash/query, render a permalinked 'Level-Up Placement' page, and generate an OG image static-export-friendly (bands packed into the hash; SVG→PNG via a tiny build-time script or client canvas). Reuse the bespoke Radar.tsx as the card art. Add dynamic OG metadata to layout.tsx. One-tap 'copy shareable link' + 'download card' on ResultsView. No backend.
items.rationale: Feature audit: fatal gap for a brand asset meant to spread. Gamification report: prestige needs a life OUTSIDE the app (LinkedIn/GitHub export) — that externalization is what makes seniors actually care. Growth loop at zero backend cost.

items.title: Make the observatory ambient everywhere (parallax starfield + atmosphere)
items.spec: The concept lives only inside the hero-viz box and two charts; 4 of 6 main views carry no observatory texture and the global background is flat #080d14 + a static grain layer with dead 0.10-opacity dots that never move (StarChart FIELD 83-85, LandingChart). Ship a fixed, GPU-cheap parallax starfield behind the whole app with subtle per-star twinkle (staggered opacity keyframes, disabled under reduced-motion) and 2-3 large blurred low-opacity radial-gradient light sources (one warm/cool source, not rainbow) for depth per the premium dark-craft report. Keep the feTurbulence grain overlay at ~4% with mix-blend-mode:overlay to kill banding. Add faint reticle/tick/crosshair guide lines at very low contrast (the instrument vocabulary). Turns the concept from stated to felt on every screen.
items.rationale: Visual audit: 'the observatory concept lives in comments and two charts, not on the surface.' Premium-UX report: layered light + grain + a single soft source is the anti-flat-and-cheap technique and the exact visual grammar of an instrument/observatory aesthetic that templates can't fake.

items.title: Interactive 'where you sit on the real ladder' comparison instrument
items.spec: The landing cites Dropbox's L4/L5 code-fluency plateau and levels.fyi as proof (page.tsx:20-22) but never delivers the 'aha' — no component places the user's own bands against those ladders. Build a hand-authored SVG instrument overlaying the learner's five band ranges onto the real public ladders (Dropbox L3-L7 with the code-fluency plateau marked as a gauge notch, Larson's four Staff archetypes as a shape selector, levels.fyi scope-of-impact axis). Hover/drag a rung to reveal that level's expectation; the user's band highlights. Ties to market report 1's core thesis: Staff+ is a change in KIND (leverage/scope), not degree — visualize scope-of-impact as the axis that grows each level, and mark Staff as a valid terminal level vs Principal as a change in kind.
items.rationale: Feature audit: 'the strongest aha the copy sets up is never delivered.' Market report 1 gives the exact source-backed ladder content (Larson archetypes, Dropbox/levels.fyi, terminal-Staff framing, the 'best senior engineer trap'). A bespoke explorable diagram is core observatory craft.

items.title: Explorable technical diagrams + reusable interactive-diagram primitive
items.spec: Diagram.tsx registry has exactly 2 static SVGs (consistency-lattice, PACELC) despite the explorable-diagram ambition. Establish a reusable interactive primitive (single React state value → SVG geometry via a pure function, Ciechanowski/Wattenberger mold) and upgrade both: PACELC becomes draggable — toggle 'partition' and watch the A-vs-C / L-vs-C branches light up; the consistency lattice becomes interactive — pick an invariant and see the weakest sufficient model highlight. Add a context-rot demo diagram for the AI track (drag context length / distractor volume, watch a hand-plotted accuracy curve degrade). Direct-manipulation, recomputes live, degrades to a meaningful static state, place numeric readouts on curves via path.getPointAtLength(). Budget best craft here — one unforgettable interactive beats ten animated cards.
items.rationale: Premium-UX report: bespoke direct-manipulation explanation is the exact bar (Ciechanowski/Wattenberger) and the hardest thing for AI/templates to fake — the site's signature, most-shared artifact. Market report 2 explicitly recommends demonstrating context rot firsthand as 'uniquely persuasive'.

items.title: Responsive + craft bug-fix pass (Nav mobile menu + logo mark, layout collapses, reduced-motion, flagship weight)
items.spec: Fix real regressions the visual audit flags as high: (a) Nav.tsx (60px fixed row, flexWrap links, no hamburger) overflows/clips at ~360px — rebuild as a responsive instrument header with a mobile menu at <720px, an authored observatory logo mark (crosshair/star glyph — currently no brand mark), and a sliding animated active-link underline; (b) proof band (page.tsx:71, hard 5fr/7fr, no media query) crushes the h2 at 360-500px — collapse like the hero does at 860px; (c) LandingChart.tsx:69-73 <animate> pulse is NOT gated on prefers-reduced-motion (violates their own CI checklist) — gate it like StarChart.tsx:164; (d) track cards (page.tsx:80/:90) render two equal tiles — give the 'Flagship' AI card real weight (larger tile, clay glow, its own mini clay/cyan constellation) so it reads as flagship, not just a border color; (e) StarChart fixed 900x560 viewBox labels collapse to ~4px on phones — add mobile label thinning.
items.rationale: These are shipped bugs on the most-seen components (Nav, landing) plus a reduced-motion violation against their own checklist — cheap correctness/craft fixes that directly serve the award-worthy + accessible bar. The logo mark gives the brand an identity it currently lacks.

items.title: Deepen + calibrate the assessment bank and per-module content
items.spec: The bank is 36 items (7/axis) with 18 orphans referenced by no module retrieval — too small to support the theta+SEM/provisional-flag machinery types.ts:106-119 promises. Author to ~15-20 items/axis against the proven CBM template (distractors = named misconceptions with per-option rationales) and wire every diagnostic item to a module retrieval set so orphans become learning hooks. Fill absent Staff-critical domains the audit lists: data modeling/schema evolution, API/contract versioning, migrations at scale, testing strategy, cost/capacity, on-call/incident depth. Give each module its own Room (fixing 7-share-room-01). Mechanical authoring against a working template, not new design.
items.rationale: Content audit rates the thin/orphaned bank 'high' — it's what makes the adaptive MST/theta claims real rather than promised. Reliable CBM needs the item count. Enables the boss-battle and roadmap items to have depth to draw on.

items.title: De-AI-fingerprinting editorial pass + reviewer honesty + model-fact currency
items.spec: Three cheap credibility fixes: (a) vary em-dash cadence (currently ~10 U+2014 per 1000 words EN, ~9 ES — the single most-cited AI fingerprint) with a light editorial pass; (b) raise Rooms' reviewers count above 1 or reword the types.ts:47 'n senior reviewers who keyed it (honesty)' claim — single-authored keys presented as senior consensus undercut the honesty schema; (c) verify the Gauntlet starter's hardcoded model id against LIVE Anthropic docs (memory: Sonnet 5 is the real 2026 model; 'claude-sonnet-4-5' reads stale to this exact audience) and prefer not hardcoding a version in learner-facing starter code.
items.rationale: Directly serves the top directive ('evitar a toda costa que se vea AI Generated'). Visual/premium report lists uniform em-dash cadence and stale model facts as precisely the tells a skeptical senior scans for. S effort, disproportionate trust payoff.

items.title: Mark learner altitude + a research-backed norm line (no leaderboard)
items.spec: The learner's position on the climb is never marked (StarChart shows static L3-L7 declination bands StarChart.tsx:126-132 but no 'you are here'). Add a glowing horizon/altitude line at the current L-band with constellations above it dimmed/locked, so every visit answers 'how far up am I' — aggregating per-module booleans into felt standing without inventing a fake number. Separately, replace the impossible/cringe client-side leaderboard with an anonymized 'norm line' on the Radar — 'where L5-ranked engineers typically place on this axis' — from static research percentiles. Competitive signal without a vanity leaderboard; reinforces diagnostic credibility.
items.rationale: Gamification audit + report: seniors hate Duolingo-style leagues/leaderboards; relatedness/status must be peer-comparison and diagnostic, not a hamster wheel. Altitude marker gives aggregate progression feel; norm line is the tasteful fourth-mechanic substitute. Both S/M and reuse existing SVG.

items.title: Harden the mastery gate + bring CBM into module retrieval
items.spec: Mastery is granted at 90% on a plain recognition MCQ with answers revealed and no cost for wrong guesses (store.ts:67, ModuleView.tsx:113-124) — trivially gameable, undercutting the prestige claim. Route the retrieval check through the existing CBM proper-scoring rule (scoring.ts:60-81) so a confident-wrong answer costs you and mastery must be earned with calibrated confidence — the product's signature CBM currently appears only in the one-time assessment (AssessRunner.tsx:173-186) and never during learning. Surface a per-module calibration trend. Pure reuse of code that already exists.
items.rationale: Gamification + feature audits: the mastery gate is the prestige bottleneck and the signature CBM mechanic vanishes after the diagnostic. Mastery-based progression gated on demonstrated competence (not clicks) is the SDT-backed model. S effort, reuses built logic.

items.title: Personalized roadmap route + re-assessment history with radar diff
items.spec: generateRoadmap() (roadmap.ts) is recomputed only inside the results hero (ResultsView.tsx:31) and thrown away — no persistent /roadmap route, no progress tracking against the prescribed sequence, and retaking overwrites the prior assessment (AssessRunner.tsx:84). Add: (a) a /roadmap page in src/app/[locale] that sequences modules from the diagnostic, tracks completion against each named behavioral delta, and re-ranks as weak axes improve — the 'definitive guide' spine the engine already computes; (b) an assessment history array on Progress (store.ts) + a radar diff view animating between takes ('Systems Judgment: Developing→Solid in 6 weeks'). Reframe Cadence as a non-punitive 'observation log' (finally write the dead cadence.weeks[] array) — a quiet sparkline of weeks with activity, never break-the-chain guilt.
items.rationale: Feature/gamification audits: engagement loop is inert (Cadence toggle writes nothing, no return hook, roadmap never surfaced). Gamification report: streaks work only as forgiving opt-in commitment devices (Cadence is that primitive) — Duolingo loss-aversion nagging is trust-destroying for seniors. The diff view is the retention hook the roadmap engine already earns.
